summary: ECOWAS citizens enter Ghana without a visa, African Union citizens apply online for an AU ETA, and a few Caribbean and Asian passports qualify for their own ETA; most other visitors need an eVisa (USD 260, up to 30 days) from the Ghana Immigration Service portal or a visa from a Ghanaian embassy.

travelInsurance.text: No insurance requirement is enforced at the border, but medical coverage including evacuation is strongly advised — well-equipped hospitals are limited outside Accra and Kumasi.

onwardTicket.text: Airlines and border officers commonly ask visa-required visitors for a confirmed return or onward ticket; keep proof of accommodation handy as well.

proofOfFunds.text: No fixed amount is published; border officers may ask visitors to show sufficient means for their stay.

currencyLimits.text: Foreign currency worth USD 10,000 or more (or the equivalent) must be declared on arrival and departure.

notes: Drones may not be brought into Ghana without prior authorization from the civil aviation authority — undeclared drones are held at the airport.

payments.text: Cards work at hotels, malls and larger restaurants in Accra and Kumasi, but cash and mobile money dominate everywhere else. Carry cedis for markets, taxis and smaller towns.

safety.text: Ghana is one of West Africa's most stable countries. Petty theft and street scams occur in Accra, and the far-northern border areas adjoining Burkina Faso call for extra caution because of regional insecurity.

bestTimeToVisit.text: November to March is the dry season — hot but with little rain; the Harmattan haze from December to February keeps skies dusty but travel easy, and December is Accra's festive peak season.

tips.text: African Union citizens outside ECOWAS are no longer visa-free: the Ghana Immigration Service portal requires an AU ETA, applied for online before travel, which replaces the visa on arrival.

Use the eligibility checker on evisa.immigration.gov.gh before you book: it tells you whether your passport needs an eVisa, an ETA or nothing at all. Ghana has run seasonal December–January visa-on-arrival schemes in past years, but the portal does not offer one.
Carry your yellow fever certificate. It is checked on arrival, and travelers without one risk on-the-spot vaccination at a fee or refusal of entry.
Malaria is present year-round throughout Ghana. Take prophylaxis, use repellent, and stick to bottled or filtered water.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Ghana?
faq.answer: It depends on your passport. ECOWAS citizens need neither a visa nor an ETA. Citizens of other African Union countries need an AU ETA, and a few Caribbean countries and Singapore have their own ETA. Most other nationalities, including the US, UK and EU, need a visa: an eVisa from the Ghana Immigration Service portal (USD 260, up to 30 days) or a visa from a Ghanaian embassy or high commission.

faq.question: Do US citizens need a visa for Ghana?
faq.answer: Yes. US passport holders need a visa before travel. They can apply online for a Ghana eVisa on the Ghana Immigration Service portal: USD 260 with standard processing within 96 hours, single entry, a stay of up to 30 days, valid 90 days from issue. A visa from a Ghanaian embassy or consulate remains an alternative.

faq.question: Is Ghana visa-free for African passport holders?
faq.answer: Only for ECOWAS citizens, who need neither a visa nor an ETA and may stay up to 90 days. Citizens of the other African Union countries must apply online for an AU ETA before travel; it is single-entry and valid for 30 days, and the portal says it replaces the visa on arrival.

faq.question: Can I get a visa on arrival in Ghana?
faq.answer: Not through the official portal. The Ghana Immigration Service eVisa portal directs visa-required travellers to an eVisa or an embassy visa before travel, and says the AU ETA replaces the visa on arrival for African Union citizens. Ghana has run seasonal December–January visa-on-arrival schemes in past years; if one is announced, confirm its terms with the Ghana Immigration Service before relying on it.

faq.question: Do I need a yellow fever vaccination for Ghana?
faq.answer: Yes. All travelers aged 9 months and over must show a valid yellow fever vaccination certificate on arrival. This applies to every nationality, including visa-free visitors.
